ar-washington-2026-candidate-list.note: A web page of tables. 182 candidate rows: 6 federal and 33 state (left to those pages), 42 county, 97 city and district, 2 judicial runoff (stored from the Secretary of State's list; read here only to compare) and 2 school runoff. Columns read: the office, the district, the municipality or school district, the candidate's name, the party and the ballot order (a number, or a mark that the candidate is unopposed). The tables also carry e-mail, address, city of residence and ZIP columns, which are never read: their cells are skipped as the page is parsed, and only the cut-down rows are kept. The SHA-256 is of the page as fetched; the page changes a little with every request, so the SHA-256 of the rows kept is given too: f982a3f34edf08430cf3c2772f54c6568cc41a09166d13e91ee5d92568bd49ce. The page also names 3 local ballot questions, which are not loaded.

ar-census-2020-place.title: 2020 Census place codes for Arkansas (st05_ar_place2020.txt)
ar-census-2020-place.note: Names, codes and counties of incorporated cities and towns only; the file has no contact data and is kept whole. A city on a county's list takes the Bureau's code and name when exactly one incorporated place of that name reaches the county.

ar-sos-2026-election-calendar.title: 2026 Election Dates (rev. June 2025)
ar-sos-2026-election-calendar.note: Checked in its text, in the order it prints them: MARCH 3, 2026; Preferential Primary Election; Nonpartisan General Election; Annual School Election; NOVEMBER 3, 2026; General Election; Nonpartisan Runoff Election; Annual School Runoff Election; DECEMBER 1, 2026; General Runoff Election (County and Municipal). The file is not kept.

ar-sbec-2026-cbec-manual.agency: Arkansas State Board of Election Commissioners
ar-sbec-2026-cbec-manual.title: 2026 County Board of Election Commissioners Procedures Manual
ar-sbec-2026-cbec-manual.note: Checked in its text: Filing - Mayor Council Form Nonpartisan Municipal Offices; the names of unopposed candidates for the office of mayor, governor, circuit clerk and non-judicial state elected officials are placed on the general election ballot separately; All unopposed candidates other than for the offices of mayor, governor, circuit clerk and non-judicial state elected officials can be declared and certified elected without being placed on the general election ballot; the phrase unopposed candidates shall appear on the ballot in a place where a voter may cast a vote for all unopposed candidates; Except for a nonpartisan election or nonpartisan municipal election, beside each candidate's name shall be his or her party designation or the term INDEPENDENT. These are what the notes on unopposed candidates and on city offices rest on (the manual cites A.C.A. 7-5-207 and 14-42-206). The file is not kept.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 Arkansas counties elect their county officers by party (county judge, sheriff, county and circuit clerks, assessor, collector, treasurer, coroner, justices of the peace and constables), and cities and towns elect the mayors, council members and other city officers whose terms are up. School boards were elected at the annual school election on March 3, 2026, and circuit judges and prosecuting attorneys at the nonpartisan general election the same day, so only their runoffs are on the November ballot. A runoff for a county or city office, where one is needed, is on December 1, 2026.
local_calendar.s: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 Election Dates (rev. June 2025), which cites A.C.A. 7-5-102, 7-10-102, 6-14-102, 6-14-121 and 7-5-106; the offices named are those on the county lists read here

local_coverage.t: Read so far: the 4 November runoffs for circuit judge and prosecuting attorney on the Secretary of State's candidate list (8 candidates; the counties of each judicial district are those of the official March 3 results); Pulaski County's contested county, constable and city contests from its election commission's ballot position draw (29 contests, 71 candidates, in the order drawn); Washington County's county, city, water district and school runoff contests from its election commission's candidate list (101 contests, 141 candidates; the 68 unopposed candidates are shown and marked). Not here yet: the other 73 of the 75 counties, each named among the gaps, and Pulaski County's offices with one candidate, which the draw leaves out. City offices are shown as nonpartisan: Pulaski County's draw lists every city candidate as Independent, Washington County's list gives no party for city offices, and no party is printed beside a name in a nonpartisan city election (A.C.A. 7-5-207). Ballot questions (constitutional issues, annexations, local option votes) are not loaded.
local_coverage.s: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 Candidate Search and official results of March 3, 2026; Pulaski County Election Commission, ballot position draw; Washington County Election Commission, candidate list; Arkansas State Board of Election Commissioners, 2026 procedures manual for county election commissioners (what the ballot prints)

gaps.w: county, city and township offices with one candidate
gaps.r: The county election commission's ballot position draw lists only contests with two or more candidates. Offices with one candidate are on the county's own candidate list, which is not loaded yet.
